QuestionStmt.S: A body cools from $60^\circ C$ to $40^\circ C$ in 6 minutes. After next 6 minutes its temperature will be (Temperature of the surroundings is $10^\circ C$)

Solution.S:
Using Newton's law of cooling in the approximate form:
$$\frac{\theta_1 - \theta_2}{t} = K \left[ \frac{\theta_1 + \theta_2}{2} - \theta_0 \right]$$
where $\theta_0 = 10^\circ C$ is the surrounding temperature.

First interval: $\theta_1 = 60^\circ C$, $\theta_2 = 40^\circ C$, $t = 6$ min.
$$\frac{60 - 40}{6} = K \left[ \frac{60 + 40}{2} - 10 \right]$$
$$\frac{20}{6} = K \times 40 \quad \Rightarrow \quad K = \frac{20}{6 \times 40} = \frac{1}{12}$$

Second interval: initial temperature $40^\circ C$, final temperature $x$, $t = 6$ min.
$$\frac{40 - x}{6} = \frac{1}{12} \left[ \frac{40 + x}{2} - 10 \right]$$
$$40 - x = \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{40 + x}{2} - 10 \right) \times 6?$$ Wait carefully:

$$\frac{40 - x}{6} = \frac{1}{12} \left( \frac{40 + x}{2} - 10 \right)$$
Multiply both sides by 6:
$$40 - x = \frac{6}{12} \left( \frac{40 + x}{2} - 10 \right) = \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{40 + x}{2} - 10 \right)$$
$$40 - x = \frac{40 + x}{4} - 5$$
Multiply by 4:
$$160 - 4x = 40 + x - 20$$
$$160 - 4x = 20 + x$$
$$160 - 20 = x + 4x$$
$$140 = 5x \quad \Rightarrow \quad x = 28^\circ C$$

Thus the temperature after the next 6 minutes is $28^\circ C$, which corresponds to option B.
